answer.evidence: All 16 conv1 kernels display classical natural image feature structures (oriented Gabor edge detectors, ridge filters, and color-opponent receptive fields) with zero-DC sums, showing no evidence of specialized patch, checkerboard, or color-noise detectors. The conv3 and FC layers exhibit balanced representations across all CIFAR-10 classes with typical weight ranges. If backdoored, class 4 (deer) is the most plausible target because it possesses the highest FC bias (+99) and a strong positive connection to conv3 channel 58 (+99, with conv3 bias +78). However, the trigger pattern and corner cannot be reliably identified as the network appears to be normally trained on clean data.
